text:
Maya: Heads up — noticed a small but consistent set of tenants getting routed to v1 even though they claimed to be on v2 in our rollout notes. acme-inc is the biggest hit. console shows implicit-route = v1. cc @Alec @Jordan
Alec: We still default to v1 when the x-redwood-version header is missing. That was the conservative choice. Is acme-inc sending headers intermittently or completely omitting?
Maya: Looks intermittent. Some requests have the header, a bunch don't. The quota shows tokens charged to v1 which is tripping their v2 usage alerts.
Jordan: Intermittent missing header -> fallback to tenant routing -> global default -> v1. We do have a special-case: if tenant has a pinned version we use that, else global default.
Sree: If we flip global default to prefer-v2 we'd affect everyone. Maybe we should add a per-tenant implicit-preference flag for the console so customers can opt their rollout cohort to prefer v2 when header absent.
Maya: Yeah, per-tenant toggle would be ideal. For now can we special-case tenants in the rollout cohort so billing/telemetry aligns?
Alec: Quick mitigation: we can set a soft-prefer flag for acme-inc in routing table to treat missing header as v2 for 30m while they finish SDK rollout. That won't change what we count as explicit v1 requests in analytics, but routing will hit v2.
Maya: That would help. Also need telemetry to surface implicit vs explicit header so we can show in the console how many requests are "silent" and being coerced. Right now the dashboard lumps them into whichever route handled them.
Jordan: I can add a tag to traces when header absent: `implicit_version=true` and `implicit_reason=missing_header`. Then dashboards can split by `implicit_version`.
Sree: Agree. We should also update quota attribution: tokens from implicit routing should be labeled `attribution=implicit` so customers understand billing differences in console billing panel.
Maya: Example header mapping logic for clarity:
```python
# simplified
version = request.headers.get('x-redwood-version')
if version:
    route = version
else:
    if tenant.flags.get('implicit_prefer_v2'):
        route = 'v2'
    else:
        route = tenant.default_version or GLOBAL_DEFAULT
```
Alec: That looks right. Two followups: 1) telemetry tag + dashboard slice 2) console affordance to set `implicit_prefer_v2` for rollout cohorts (opt-in) 3) short-term routing override for acme-inc. I can do 3 now.
console-bot: Banner draft: "Missing client version header? Enable implicit v2 preference for this tenant so you don't get routed to legacy endpoints during SDK rollout. Learn more -> /docs/implicit-versioning"
Maya: Banner copy looks fine. Make it tasteful — don't surprise billing. Add an explicit note that "this only affects routing; billing attribution will show implicit vs explicit until we change policy".
Jordan: Telemetry query we can add to the monitoring runbook (example):
```sql
-- implicit header counts per tenant, last 1h
SELECT tenant_id, routed_version, count(*) as requests, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM request_events
WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '1 hour' AND coalesce(headers['x-redwood-version'], '') = ''
GROUP BY tenant_id, routed_version
ORDER BY tokens desc
```
Maya: Perfect. Ops question: if we flip routing to v2 for missing headers, do we risk silent quality regressions? e.g., v2 may break older clients.
Alec: That's why the per-tenant opt-in is safest. For the short-term per-tenant override we do a canary: route X% of implicit traffic to v2 and sample outputs for evals. If no major regression in 10k tokens we can increase.
Sree: Suggestion: add an automatic fallback for errors where v2 returns 5xx -> route back to v1 for that request and tag it `fallback_on_error=true`. That keeps apps from failing while we help customers roll out.
Maya: Yes please — fallback_on_error should also increment an alert counter so we can detect increased regressions.
ops-bot: deploy: routing-override-for-acme-inc started by Alec — probe=true, initial-weight=30%%, window=30m
Alec: I'll follow up with a console feature PR for the implicit toggle and the billing note. Jordan will wire the telemetry tags. Sree can add the fallback-on-error and evaluation sampling.
Maya: Thanks team. Once the probe shows stable routing and telemetry slices look sane, we'll notify the customer and recommend they enable the console toggle while they finish SDK rollout. :thumbsup:
Jordan: Filing a tiny runbook item to check implicit vs explicit split and token-attribution daily for 48h.
Maya: Action items summarized:
- Alec: short-term routing override for acme-inc (in progress)
- Jordan: telemetry tags + dashboard slice for implicit requests
- Sree: fallback-on-error + sampling eval hook
- Alec: console banner + per-tenant `implicit_prefer_v2` toggle PR
- Maya: coordinate with customer success to notify acme-inc after 30m probe
Alec: on it.
ops-bot: deploy: routing-override-for-acme-inc completed — status=active, probe-weight=30%%
Maya: Closing loop: first 15 minutes look good, errors unchanged, tokens routed to v2 for implicit hits. Will re-evaluate at 30m and then decide whether to flip the toggle or ramp down.
